html_en:
Agents are no longer a future-tense concept — from browser automation to personal finance, the infrastructure for AI acting on your behalf is quietly going live, and the economic implications are only beginning to sink in.

🌐 Claude Leaves the Sandbox: Browser Agents Go Mainstream

The most significant product launch of the day came from Anthropic, which announced that Claude in Chrome is now generally available on every paid plan. The feature lets Claude read pages, click links, fill forms, and navigate the web using your existing logins — crucially, it can now do so without asking permission for every single action.

The real engineering story here is the prompt injection defense. Malicious actors can hide instructions inside web pages or emails to trick an AI agent into acting against you — imagine asking Claude to draft email replies, only for a hidden instruction to forward your inbox to an attacker. Anthropic's response is a layered system: models trained against a growing library of attacks, probes that screen web content before Claude acts on it, and action-level classifiers that verify each move against your original request before it executes.

"On our initial evaluation testing Claude's resilience against prompt injection attacks, no attack succeeded against Claude Fable 5, Claude Opus 5, or Claude Sonnet 5 in the Cowork harness, even without the probes and classifiers." — Anthropic blog

The pitch is compelling: all those internal dashboards, legacy vendor portals, and systems that never got an API integration? Claude can now just... use them like a human would.

💸 The Agent Economy: Who Wins When AI Does the Spending?

A thread running through today's feed is the dawning realization that agents aren't just productivity tools — they're becoming the primary interface for commerce. Peter Yang shared a telling anecdote from the ChatGPT Finances product lead:

"I used points to book a hotel, and then they still billed me. I had no idea it happened but ChatGPT caught it, worked with customer service, and I ended up getting reimbursed." — Ethan, via @petergyang

Yang himself went further, describing how he had ChatGPT autonomously cancel a hotel booking for his parents, monitor replies, and follow up until the refund came through. His broader take was blunt: "I no longer live in email or text, I live in the chat with my agent(s)."

Box CEO Aaron Levie offered the most expansive framing of the day, sketching out why agent commerce could be genuinely transformative:

"You'll start by slinging your daily simple and annoying tasks at the agent. Then as people get used to it, they'll just start to throw more complex tasks at the agent, ultimately leading to even more spend through these systems than what they were doing before. If you can bring down the friction for commerce and services, then you end up spending even more." — @levie

And on the infrastructure side, Levie noted that the platforms managing data, security guardrails, and business logic for agents have an enormous opening: "AI agents will use software 100X more than people ever did."

📉 The Ad Industry's Quiet Crisis

If agents are doing the browsing, who sees the ads? Peter Yang raised the uncomfortable question that the digital advertising industry hasn't yet fully grappled with:

"If a huge part of your business is showing targeted display ads to humans — what happens when agents browse your website and get the job done without a human seeing your ads at all?" — @petergyang

It's an elegant statement of a structural problem. The entire programmatic advertising edifice — retargeting, display, behavioral tracking — is predicated on human eyeballs following human intent through a browser. Agent-mediated browsing breaks every assumption in that chain. The reckoning may not be imminent, but it's coming.

⚙️ The Agentic Coding Race Heats Up

On the developer tools front, Garry Tan emerged as an unlikely evangelist for Capy, a newer agentic coding tool:

"Not really sure how @capydotai does it, but it really is able to track multi-step workflow and do large PRs faster than Codex or Claude Code on its own. My most favorite new agentic coding secret weapon in my arsenal the last week." — @garrytan

Meanwhile, Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch was impressed by a different model entirely: "I just gave Grok 4.7 a pretty hard problem, involving reverse-engineering a running binary. Beautifully solved. And it's so fast!" — a notable endorsement from someone who lives at the frontier of developer tooling.

Nikunj offered a useful corrective to the hype around context-window maximalism:

"With a few exceptions, the companies boasting about tokenmaxxing have the worst product experiences. It's because good products are all about curation & gardening and not throwing the kitchen sink at agents expecting them to figure it out. Less is more has never been more apt." — @nikunj

And the broader agentic coding ecosystem got a moment of third-party validation: @steipete clarified the circulating "Meta uses OpenClaw" story — Meta built their own agent inspired by the approach, not a direct fork — while also noting a cleaner advantage of self-hosting: "The beauty of running a claw yourself: they cannot block you."

✨ One to Watch

@thsottiaux's cryptic Tuesday teaser — "start your engines... I promised a reset for Tuesday" — drew 12,500 likes with no context whatsoever. Whatever it is, the AI community is paying attention. And Amjad Masad of Replit kept it simple: "AI is reviving the American Dream." Given that Replit's entire thesis is democratizing software creation, it's less a boast than a mission statement.

Watch/Listen: Latent Space Pod — new episode out now (Apple Podcasts, YouTube, email)
html_zh:
AI智能体正在从开发者工具悄然演变为日常生活的基础设施——从浏览器自动化到个人财务管理，一场关于"谁来主导智能体经济"的竞争已经悄然展开。

🧠 Claude 进驻浏览器：Anthropic 的"最后一公里"战略

本周最值得关注的产品动态，来自 Anthropic。Claude in Chrome 正式向所有付费用户全面开放，标志着浏览器级 AI 智能体从实验走向普及。这不只是一个功能更新，而是 Anthropic 在"无集成"场景下的关键押注——那些没有 API、没有原生接入的内部仪表盘、遗留系统和供应商门户，Claude 现在都可以直接操作。

更关键的是安全机制的成熟。Anthropic 在博文中详细披露了其对抗"提示注入攻击"的防御体系：

"在提示注入攻击中，恶意行为者将指令隐藏在网页内容、电子邮件或表单字段中。你可能永远不会看到它们，但这些指令可以将智能体重定向，让它做你从未要求的事情。"
— Claude 官方博客

Anthropic 表示，在最新评测中，针对 Claude Sonnet 5、Opus 5 和 Fable 5 的所有注入攻击均未成功。这是一个实质性的安全里程碑，也是他们敢于全面开放的底气所在。

💸 智能体经济的两面：广告业的噩梦，商务层的盛宴

当智能体真正开始替人类"上网干活"，整个数字经济的底层逻辑都在动摇。@petergyang 抛出了一个令广告业不安的问题：

"如果你的生意依赖于向人类展示定向展示广告，那当智能体替人浏览网站、完成任务，而根本没有人类看到你的广告时，会发生什么？"
— @petergyang

但硬币的另一面，却是巨大的商业机遇。@levie（Box CEO Aaron Levie）给出了他对"智能体商务层"的预判，逻辑清晰且令人信服：

"个人智能体代表你进行交易，其货币化潜力相当可观。你一开始会把简单烦人的任务扔给智能体，随着人们习以为常，会开始交付更复杂的任务，最终通过这些系统产生的消费甚至会超过以前的水平。如果你能降低商务和服务的摩擦，人们反而会消费更多。"
— @levie

@levie 还进一步指出，智能体使用软件的频率将是人类的 100 倍，这让 CRM、ERP 等核心数据平台的价值不降反升——前提是它们能成为智能体的安全护栏和编排层。

ChatGPT 的财务功能已经给出了具体案例。@petergyang 分享了 ChatGPT Finances 产品负责人 Ethan 的亲身经历：

"我用积分订了酒店，但他们还是扣了我的款。我完全不知道，是 ChatGPT 发现的，它跟客服沟通，最终帮我拿回了钱。"
— Ethan，ChatGPT Finances 产品负责人

⚙️ 编码智能体军备竞赛：Grok 4.7 惊艳亮相，Capy 成新宠

在开发者工具赛场，本周同样热闹。@rauchg（Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch）对 Grok 4.7 的表现给出了罕见的高评价：

"我刚刚给 Grok 4.7 出了一道很难的题，涉及对运行中二进制文件的逆向工程。解得漂亮，而且速度极快！"
— @rauchg

与此同时，@garrytan（Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan）将 Capy 称为他近一周内最喜欢的"秘密武器"：

"不太确定 @capydotai 是怎么做到的，但它真的能追踪多步骤工作流，处理大型 PR 的速度比单独用 Codex 或 Claude Code 都快。这是我最近一周最喜欢的新编码智能体秘密武器。"
— @garrytan

产品设计层面，@nikunj 则对"token 堆砌"风气提出了批评：

"少数例外之外，那些吹嘘 tokenmaxxing 的公司往往产品体验最差……好产品的核心是筛选与打磨，而不是把所有东西都扔给智能体然后期待它自己搞明白。'少即是多'从未如此贴切。"
— @nikunj

🌟 散点观察：美国梦、提示词习惯与神秘的周二预告

几个值得记录的边角料：@amasad（Replit CEO）简短有力地写道"AI 正在复兴美国梦"，配上一篇文章链接，引发近 600 个点赞的共鸣。

社交媒体上流传最广的"生产力 hack"，却意外地朴素。@trq212 写道：

"我现在每天要打好几遍'用大图、少文字'这句话。"
— @trq212

一万七千个点赞说明，与 AI 协作时最有效的指令，往往不是最复杂的那个。

最后，悬念留给了 @thsottiaux——这位神秘账号以 12000+ 点赞的帖子预告"周二将有重大重置"。AI 圈正屏息等待。Watch/Listen: Latent Space Podcast 最新一期也已上线，感兴趣的读者可移步收听。
